chosen.title: Single Kettlebell Rack Carry
chosen.description:
Key points for the Single Kettlebell Rack Carry:
+ load kettlebell on your forearm
+ thumb close to the sternum 
+ chest stays lifted up towards kettlebell
+ drive the elbow up creating a shelf for the kettlebell to rest in
+ keep your wrist flat
+ constantly push up into that kettlebell
+ walk slowly and don't collapse, stay tall

candidates.title: How to Properly Perform a Kettlebell Rack | Dr. Andy Chen #shorts
candidates.description:
Rack position is the foundation for all kettlebell movements.

The one thing that I always coach is this position because no one knows how to do it right.

If you keep the elbows on your torso, you’ll have the tendency to lean when you get fatigued.

Try to keep the arms off the torso so you use an active strategy.

If you fatigue then you’ll take the passive one but if you’re using the passive one from the start then what happens next?

candidates.title: The CORRECT way to hold the kettlebell front rack✅
candidates.description:
🔥The Front Rack: Do’s and Dont’s🔥

The front rack position while really basic is a very important part of maximizing your kettlebell training✅

I see a lot of messy front racks floating around the inter webs so let me break from the proper front in these very easy to follow steps✅

1️⃣Have the handle of the kettlebell cutting across the meaty part of your hand

2️⃣Point your knuckles to the ceiling and have a strong wrist 

3️⃣Keep your elbow as tight to your body as possible and keep a vertical forearm

candidates.title: MUST TRY UNDERRATED EXERCISE! (FARMERS WALK EXPLAINED)
candidates.description:
Get your FREE form guide here- https://colossusfitness.lpages.co/form-cheat-sheet/

You ever do these? 🤔 👇

The Farmer’s walk is an incredible highly underrated exercise. 🙌

It’s a full body exercise that can improve muscle strength and power, as well as cardiovascular health and endurance.

It also stimulates a number of muscle groups, including the legs, glutes, upper back, traps, lats, abs, biceps, forearms, hand muscles & more. 💪

Here are some cues:
🔥 Pick up your dumbbells
🔥 Keep your chest up & shoulders back
🔥 Engage your core by keeping it nice and tight
🔥 Walk in a straight line, and take small controlled steps
🔥Don’t lean – keep your torso straight, avoid tipping side to side.

Give these a try and let me know how it goes.

#gymmotivation #fitnessmotivation #healthylifestyle

candidates.title: How to Properly Hold a Kettlebell in the Rack Position #kettlebellworkouts #strengthtrainingforwomen
candidates.description:
The rack position is used for many kettlebell exercises, and it can be a little tricky to get your set up right. 

Here are 7 key points to keep in mind: 

1️⃣ Hand fully inserted through the kettlebell handle. 2️⃣ Handle rests on the outside of the forearm 
3️⃣ Handle diagonal across the palm. 
4️⃣ Wrist straight. 
5️⃣ Fingers relaxed. 
6️⃣ Kettlebell in the V of the shoulder, elbow, and hand. 7️⃣ Kettlebell rests against the body. There are many OTHER ways to hold a kettlebell besides the rack position. 

Want to learn more about the different ways to hold a kettlebell and how to incorporate it into your training? Comment “handle” below. ⬇️

candidates.title: How to Properly Rack a Kettlebell
candidates.description:
Like all strength training movements, mastery of training with kettlebells comes with time and quality practice. Keeping the weights light while you learn proper technique, maintaining good positions, and working through a full range of motion will ensure steady progression toward your training goals. The foundational kettlebell exercises such as the deadlift, squat, hinge, swing, clean, clean & press, and snatch – are no exception. 

One of the most overlooked techniques of training with kettlebells is how to properly rack the kettlebell. The rack is where the kettlebell ends up after the clean and serves as the transition between the clean and pressing the kettlebell overhead to a locked position (or bringing it back down from overhead).

Check out this video where I demonstrate how to create a more efficient racked position. This can completely change your kettlebell training and help you quickly improve your technique and transitions.
